reference.title: Barbell Seated Front Raise
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be fetched from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you raise, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.8 s up, short pause, about 2 s down

prescription.load: User-chosen barbell load; light (an empty or light fixed bar is often enough).

cues.text: Sit tall on the end of a flat bench, feet flat. Hold the bar overhand about shoulder width apart, resting just above the thighs, arms straight with soft elbows.
Breathe out and raise the bar straight forward and up with nearly straight arms.
Stop at shoulder height; chest up, no lean back, shoulders down away from the ears.
Lower slowly in about 2 s back to just above the thighs.
Brief pause without resting the bar on the legs; repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Rocking back to swing the bar up
mistakes.fix: Sit tall and still; lighter bar.
Stop at about shoulder height (clinical opinion).

mistakes.mistake: Bending the elbows into a curl
mistakes.fix: Keep the arms nearly straight, elbows soft.
Keep the shoulders down and the neck long.

kinematics.norm: From the bar over the thighs to about 90 degrees (the top of the range tested by Coratella 2020)
Overhand, about shoulder width (clinical opinion); the frontal raise loads the anterior deltoid most among the raises compared in Campos 2020
Upright on the end of a flat bench, feet flat (clinical opinion)
2 s up, 0.5 s pause, 2 s down in Coratella 2020

sources.title: GymVisual, Barbell Seated Front Raise, video (movement reference)
Coratella et al. 2020, an electromyographic analysis of lateral raise variations and frontal raise in competitive bodybuilders (Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(17):6015)
Campos et al. 2020, different shoulder exercises affect the activation of deltoid portions in resistance-trained individuals (J Hum Kinet 75:5-14)

cautions: Shoulder pain: lower only to a pain-free height, or use a lighter bar (clinical opinion).
Keep the trunk still; leaning back shifts the load to the lower back.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: a neutral-grip dumbbell raise or a smaller range.

muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Main mover: shoulder flexion. The frontal raise gave the highest anterior deltoid activity in the lifting phase among the raises tested (Coratella 2020; standing, dumbbells).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Main mover: shoulder flexion. The frontal raise gave the highest anterior deltoid activity in the lifting phase among the raises tested (Coratella 2020; standing, dumbbells).
muscleNotes.pec_r: The clavicular head helps flex the shoulder; it was most active in the frontal raise (Coratella 2020).
muscleNotes.pec_l: The clavicular head helps flex the shoulder; it was most active in the frontal raise (Coratella 2020).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Helps hold the arms up; medial deltoid activity was lower in the frontal raise than in lateral raises (Coratella 2020).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Helps hold the arms up; medial deltoid activity was lower in the frontal raise than in lateral raises (Coratella 2020).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Upward rotation of the shoulder blades as the arms rise.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Upward rotation of the shoulder blades as the arms rise.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Supports the shoulder blades near the top.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Supports the shoulder blades near the top.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff: keeps the ball of the shoulder centred.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Rotator cuff: keeps the ball of the shoulder centred.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Keep the spine tall against the load in front.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Keep the spine tall against the load in front.
muscleNotes.core: Holds the trunk still; no rocking back on the seat.
